author: Press Association
description:
Rock band will still tour the UK, Europe and US over the next year but say decision to ‘fall dormant’ feels ‘liberating’

The British rock band Enter Shikari have announced they will go on hiatus at the end of 2027, a decision that may result in the band’s “extinction”.

The St Albans band, who formed in 1999 as Hybryd, are due to tour the UK in November, Europe and the US next year, and said they hoped to play some of their favourite places “one last time”.

Continue reading...
title: Enter Shikari announce indefinite hiatus from 2027: ‘We don’t think we’re splitting up’

author: Patrick Greenfield
description:
After five years of work, 5,750 panels of toughened glass will help keep hundred of plants safe from Scottish winters – but more work needs to be done

In the early autumn sunlight, Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh’s extensive plant collection appears safe in their glass enclosures. But danger lurks from above for the tropical ferns, cycads and rare alpine heathers.

Soon the September sunshine will give way to the storms and gales of the Scottish winter, which can bring hundreds of glass panels crashing to the greenhouse floor on the windiest days. Nobody is allowed inside when the wind is above 30mph.

Continue reading...
title: Falling glass and ‘decapitated’ plants: the race to protect Edinburgh botanic garden’s plants

author: Alba Asenjo Domínguez
description:
Landlords can no longer refuse pit bulls, rottweilers, dobermans or other breeds considered ‘scary’

Landlords in Washington DC will no longer be able to refuse a tenant’s dog based on its breed, size or weight, nor can they impose special charges related to these factors.

At least, that’s what a new law that took effect on Thursday aims to achieve. Animal welfare organizations and animal shelters applauded the legislation, emphasizing the benefits of reducing barriers to pet ownership in the US capital.

Continue reading...
title: New Washington DC law bans landlords from imposing dog breed restrictions

author: Associated Press
description:
Democratic-led coalition says gutting key protections will set US back decades and worsen climate crisis

States and cities sued the Trump administration on Thursday for repealing rules that limit planet-warming greenhouse gas emissions from power plants fueled by coal and natural gas.

Twenty-one states, led by New York, are challenging the Environmental Protection Agency’s power plant rule. The Democratic-led coalition also includes Pennsylvania’s governor, the District of Columbia, New York City, Chicago and the city and county of Denver. They argue that “gutting one of the country’s most significant climate protections” will set the nation back decades and worsen the climate crisis.

Continue reading...
title: US states and cities sue over Trump EPA’s repeal of emissions rules

author: Abené Clayton
description:
MLB reportedly contacted White House about staging game at Wyoming park, to dismay of locals and conservationists

A proposal to hold a Major League Baseball (MLB) game inside a national park is receiving backlash from locals and conservationists.

On 26 September, the Washington Post reported that MLB reached out to the White House about staging a one-day game at the Grand Teton national park in Wyoming. Teton county describes itself as a “a year-round resort community” and sits within the Jackson Hole valley. It’s also a habitat for grizzly bears, osprey, bison and more.

Continue reading...
title: Proposal to hold Major League Baseball game in Grand Teton national park sparks backlash

author: Nadeem Badshah
description:
Planned rule change forms part of Burnham’s bid to crack down on the ‘little charges that add up’

Airlines will be blocked from charging parents extra to sit with their children on planes, according to government plans.

The new rule would require airlines to seat passengers aged under 14 next to their parents or an accompanying adult free of charge. Passengers will also no longer need to pay to tweak the name on their flight booking if they need to correct a mistake.

Continue reading...
title: UK airlines to be banned from charging parents to sit with children

author: Nick Visser
description:
Follow the day’s news live.

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Former Wallaby hooker Nathan Charles diagnosed with MND at 37

The former Wallaby Nathan Charles, who became the first cystic fibrosis sufferer in the world to play a contact sport professionally, has been diagnosed with motor neurone disease (MND).

Continue reading...
title: Australia news live: eSafety warns online gaming can cause ‘serious harms’ to children; Atlassian to power solar farm

author: Guardian staff
description:
Shoppers and vendors in Aspen surprised by unusual customer as it stretched to sample stall offerings

Farmers’ market shoppers might not usually pay much attention to the local resident devouring fresh bread and pastries at one of the stalls with extra gusto – but some certainly did last weekend when they realized it was a hungry bear.

Onlookers on Saturday reached for their phones to take photos and videos of the bear in downtown Aspen, Colorado, after it wandered through the stalls and got up on to its hind legs to dig into the baked goods.

Continue reading...
title: Hitting the sweet spot: bear treats itself to baked goods at Colorado farmers’ market

author: Associated Press
description:
Request for Clancy, 36, to be acquitted turned down nearly a month after first trial ended with deadlocked jury

The judge in the Lindsay Clancy murder case on Thursday refused to declare her not guilty, turning down a defense motion that had argued there was not enough evidence to prove she was responsible for killing her three children.

On Tuesday, Clancy’s attorney Kevin Reddington tried to persuade Judge William Sullivan that prosecutors had not offered any proof that Clancy had killed her three children. Prosecutors argued there was plenty of evidence, calling Reddington’s claim “laughable”.

Continue reading...
title: Judge denies defense motion to declare Lindsay Clancy not guilty of murder

author: Ariana Baio
description:
Court will review practice of indefinite detention for undocumented immigrants living in the US

The US supreme court agreed on Thursday to take up a case challenging the Trump administration’s practice of indefinite detention for undocumented immigrants living in the US and awaiting deportation proceedings.

At the center of the immigration case is a dispute over Donald Trump’s reinterpretation of a longstanding policy that has led to a huge surge in the number of migrants held in detention centers.

Continue reading...
title: Supreme court to hear case challenging Trump’s immigration detention policy

author: Reuters
description:
State attorney general issues subpoena to OpenAI as ​part of broader inquiry into potential security vulnerabilities

California’s attorney general has issued an investigative subpoena to OpenAI, starting an investigation into the startup ⁠as ​part of a broader inquiry into potential cybersecurity vulnerabilities and incidents related ⁠to its AI models, his office said on Thursday.

Last month, Rob Bonta announced that ⁠the Department of Justice was conducting a formal ​investigation into the “Hugging ‌Face incident”, amid increasing ‌scrutiny of the AI industry. AI agents developed by OpenAI hacked Hugging Face in July, gaining access to parts of the open-source platform’s infrastructure.

Continue reading...
title: California issues investigative subpoena to OpenAI over rogue agents’ hacking

author: Josh Halliday North of England editor
description:
PM has praised Abu Dhabi group as ‘huge partner’ in reshaping Manchester, but critics say this ignores public cost of city’s transformation

In July 2016, the Manchester City player Yaya Touré ambled into a small bar near Beijing’s Workers’ Stadium and offered a bemused smile as dozens of Chinese fans rushed towards him.

Manchester City had just won their sixth trophy under the big-spending ownership of Sheikh Mansour’s Abu Dhabi United Group and the blues were international megastars. They were also magnets for investment.

Continue reading...
title: How success of Manchester City helped put Andy Burnham in power

author: Rowena Mason, Pippa Crerar and Patrick Butler
description:
Exclusive: Plan under discussion involves intensive support to help young people into employment

Ministers are working up sweeping plans for welfare changes including scrapping a key disability benefit for under-25s and replacing it with a multibillion-pound package of support to get into work, the Guardian has learned.

Whitehall sources said the package of changes under debate was much bigger than previously thought, as Andy Burnham’s government hopes to persuade more people on benefits back into work.

Continue reading...
title: Key disability benefit for young people may be axed under major welfare changes

author: Jessica Elgot,Heather Stewart, Pippa Crerar and Richard Partington
description:
Chancellor faces global volatility and soaring energy costs as some insiders worry lack of clarity could trigger fresh market shock

Senior Labour figures are privately voicing unease about John Healey’s approach to his crucial first budget this month, against the backdrop of volatile global markets and soaring energy costs.

The chancellor’s work has been made significantly harder by the global bond sell-off, which continues to raise the cost of government borrowing, and ever increasing energy prices as Donald Trump continues the US war with Iran.

Continue reading...
title: Labour figures uneasy about Healey’s ‘underpowered’ approach to budget

author: Ben Beaumont-Thomas
description:
Singer and bassist helped turn Newcastle band into hugely influential force on thrash and black metal subgenres

Conrad Lant, the British heavy metal musician who fronted Venom and ensured the Newcastle band became a huge influence on the genre, has died aged 63.

“For more than four decades, Conrad’s voice, bass and vision were at the heart of Venom,” reads a statement from the band. “He created something that changed heavy music for ever. Venom never followed the rules. They forged their own path. And Conrad was there at the centre of it all – uncompromising, fearless and unmistakable.” No cause of death was given.

Continue reading...
title: Conrad ‘Cronos’ Lant, frontman of UK heavy metal band Venom, dies aged 63

author: Aram Roston in Washington
description:
Installing tech billionaires Elon Musk and Palmer Luckey to Pentagon defense board raises conflict of interest concerns

By installing the tech billionaires Elon Musk and Palmer Luckey to advisory roles in a Pentagon project about the future of warfare, the defense secretary, Pete Hegseth, bestowed extraordinary influence on two of Maga’s most significant campaign donors – and both men own companies that benefit from federal defense contracting.

The new project, which Hegseth dubbed “Project Meridian” in an event in Quantico, Virginia, on Wednesday, will be led by Pentagon official Emil Michael, a former Uber executive. As the Guardian has reported, Michael made millions in profits off non-public Musk company AI stock while in federal office – and while guiding the Department o
title: Hegseth puts the future of warfare in the hands of major Maga donors

author: Jamie Grierson
description:
Counter-terrorism police arrest 27-year-old in Westminster, while second man questioned under caution

Detectives have arrested a dual UK-Iranian national on suspicion of terrorism offences as part of an investigation into a suspected plot near RAF Fairford.

Counter-terrorism police said the 27-year-old man was arrested on Thursday in Westminster on suspicion of preparation of terrorist acts under section 5 of the Terrorism Act 2006.

Continue reading...
title: UK-Iran national arrested under Terrorism Act over RAF Fairford incident

author: Alex Daniel
description:
Ministers discuss drawing down EU countries’ reserves after Donald Trump threatens to cut off US supplies

Britain is in talks with European allies over releasing emergency diesel stockpiles after Donald Trump threatened to cut off US supplies of the fuel.

Ministers held calls with counterparts from the European Commission, Germany, France, Italy and Ireland on Thursday to discuss whether to draw down reserves after the Trump administration told Germany and France to release their stockpiles to help ease soaring global energy prices or face a US export ban.

Continue reading...
title: Britain in talks with European allies over release of emergency diesel stockpiles

author: Alba Asenjo Domínguez
description:
Wife and brother of Minneapolis woman killed in immigration crackdown allege wrongful death

The family of Renee Good, the woman killed by immigration agents in January in Minneapolis, filed two federal lawsuits against the agent who shot her and several top officials in the Trump administration on Thursday.

In the lawsuits, Good’s partner, Becca Good, and her brother, Brent Ganger, alleged wrongful death and other violations of federal law, according to a press release issued by their lawyers.

Continue reading...
title: Family of Renee Good sues ICE agent who shot her and top Trump officials

author: Ellie Violet Bramley
description:
Collaboration regarded as ‘really big thing’ for retailer in some quarters despite backlash around designer’s antisemitic remarks in 2011

A month after it was announced that a planned exhibition dedicated to fashion designer John Galliano at New York’s Metropolitan Museum of Art would not proceed, his debut collection for fast fashion company Zara has been released.

Called Re{form}, it was, according to a press release, “authored by the couturier John Galliano. Built from our memory. Made for now.”

Continue reading...
title: Terrible idea or major coup? Galliano’s Zara collection launches after Met controversy

author: Michael Savage Media editor
description:
West Ham co-owner and former pornographer lodges high court claim over episode, in which several women accused him of abusing power

David Sullivan is suing the BBC for £150m over multiple claims of sexual misconduct made in a documentary.

Lawyers acting for Sullivan, who remains West Ham United’s co-owner, have lodged a high court claim against the corporation over its Panorama investigation Predator: The Billionaire Football Boss, which was broadcast in June.

Continue reading...
title: David Sullivan sues BBC for £150m over Panorama’s sexual misconduct claims

author: Ariana Baio
description:
President also doesn’t rule out declaring state of emergency before midterms and deflects responsibility for Iran war

  • US politics live – latest updates

Donald Trump deflected responsibility for misleading Americans about the length of the Iran war, dismissed low poll ratings as “fake numbers” and refused to rule out the possibility of declaring a state of emergency before the midterms, in a wide-ranging interview with Time magazine.

When confronted with questions about the length of the Iran war, the US president blamed the media for reporting his remarks in which
title: Trump dismisses low poll ratings as ‘fake numbers’ in Time interview

author: Henry Belot
description:
One executive received a $1.5m package last year, while 10 other staff received remuneration exceeding $1m each

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Nearly a dozen federal public servants were paid more than $1m last year, with one receiving a $1.5m package worth more than double Anthony Albanese’s base salary.

The generous remuneration – which includes bonuses and allowances – has been criticised as insulting during a cost-of-living crisis and amid job cuts across the public service.

Continue reading...
title: Million-dollar public servants: 11 staff at Australia’s Future Fund paid significantly more than the PM

author: Donna Lu Assistant editor, climate, environment and science
description:
Melbourne researchers behind previous BV transmission breakthrough turn attention to understanding why some cases are harder to cure

Australian scientists have identified two contributors to recurrent bacterial vaginosis infections, a common sexual health condition that affects about one in four women globally.

The condition, commonly called BV, is characterised by an imbalance of naturally occurring bacteria in the vagina, in which there is a reduction of “good” bacteria and an overgrowth of other mixed bacteria.

Continue reading...
title: Underlying causes of recurrent bacterial vaginosis identified by Australian scientists

author: Adam Morton, Graham Readfearn and Penry Buckley
description:
Exclusive: Climate Change Authority chair says planning commission did not account for climate-related economic damage in NSW

  • Sign up for climate and environment editor Adam Morton’s free Clear Air newsletter here

A senior Albanese government climate adviser has challenged the state approval of the largest coalmining development in New South Wales’ history, arguing “climate change isn’t someone else’s problem”.

Matt Kean, the chair of the Climate Change Authority and a former NSW treasurer and energy minister, questioned why the state Independent Planning Commission had not weighed the economic cost of climate change caused by burning the coal from the
title: Matt Kean warns climate crisis ‘isn’t someone else’s problem’ as largest coal project in NSW history greenlit

author: Josh Butler
description:
Maker of Claude claims AI could transform economy but ABC and SBS say the technology should be subject to media regulations

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

AI giant Anthropic has urged the Albanese government to consider giving “conditional approval” for big tech to train its models on Australian copyrighted works under an opt-out model, after conceding it won’t secure a blanket copyright exemption.

But Australia’s public broadcasters, the ABC and SBS, have strongly criticised AI firms, calling on the government to enact strict new rules to compensate media organisations and protect public interest journalism.
title: Anthropic pushes for opt-out model for Australian content as ABC warns of ‘cannibalisation’ of news

author: Jeremy Barr in Washington
description:
Network was listed as primary TV pool covering Thursday’s presidential activities but then was abruptly removed

For a second time in a week, the White House has unilaterally removed CNN from its assignment as the primary television pool representative covering Donald Trump.

CNN was excluded on Saturday from pool duty aboard Air Force One, despite a district judge’s ruling – two days earlier – overturning the White House’s ban on the network and two other media organizations.

Continue reading...
title: White House removes CNN from press pool for second time in a week

author: Andrew Pulver
description:
Decision follows independent review into handling of February ceremony, where his involuntary tics caused a BBC crisis

John Davidson, the Tourette syndrome campaigner whose outburst at the British Academy film awards in February led to a crisis for Bafta (British Academy of Film and Television Arts) and the BBC, will attend the Bafta Scotland awards and watch the ceremony from a separate “relaxed” space.

In a letter sent to Bafta members on Thursday, the organisation’s chair Sara Putt and CEO Jane Millichip said that, after an independent review, Bafta had “strengthened and centralised our safeguarding, risk assessment and compliance processes” and had made arrangements in consultation with “safeguarding and inclus
title: Tourette syndrome campaigner John Davidson to watch Bafta Scotland awards in separate ‘relaxed’ space

author: Alba Asenjo Domínguez
description:
Witnesses in the chamber said Christa Pike was still breathing despite receiving injections intended to kill her

When the prison warden asked Christa Pike if she had any last words, she said she was going to leave this world “with love” for those on her side and also the ones angry with her.

What followed was the second botched execution in Tennessee this year, after two doses of the lethal injection failed to produce the desired effect.

Continue reading...
title: Witnesses detail horror of Tennessee woman’s botched execution: ‘None of it was normal’

author: Abené Clayton
description:
Administration says increased immigration enforcement led to fewer homicides, but they have been on the decline since Joe Biden’s term

Over the last year and a half, the US has seen a historic drop in homicides. Researchers and reporters are still puzzling through the complex set of reasons why - from the easing of pandemic-era stressors and the Biden administration’s investments in community-based violence prevention to policing and other factors.

But for the Trump administration, there’s one easy explanation: increased immigration enforcement. As the midterm elections approach, the White House has been doubling down on this message, saying its crackdown against immigrants is why US crime rates are now falling.

Continue reading...
title: Trump and his allies credit deportations with record low crime. Experts disagree

author: Matthew Weaver
description:
London schoolgirl’s father taught her to play when she was five, and three years later she beat former British champion

Over the weekend, 11-year-old Bodhana Sivanandan became the youngest ever holder of the title of woman grandmaster at the Chess Olympiad in Uzbekistan while playing on a car booster seat so she could reach the board. By Tuesday morning she was back at school in north London for a design and technology lesson.

Bodhana has to juggle the competing pressures of being an international chess sensation with the more ordinary challenges of childhood and her first term at secondary school.

Continue reading...
title: ‘I do it because I like it’: Bodhana Sivanandan, 11, on being youngest ever ‘woman grandmaster’

author: Richard Luscombe
description:
Independent inquiry ordered after halted execution of Pike, who was convicted of murder

Tennessee’s governor has suspended all executions in the state until at least the end of the year and ordered an independent inquiry after a botched attempt to put a condemned inmate to death on Wednesday night.

Witnesses at the execution chamber in Nashville said Christa Pike, who was convicted of murder, was still awake and snoring loudly about 40 minutes after officials administered two doses of the lethal drug pentobarbital.

Continue reading...
title: Tennessee governor suspends all executions after Christa Pike’s lethal injections fail

author: Gwyn Topham Transport correspondent
description:
Driver of East Midlands train, who died in June crash, received automatic warning after passing red light but train continued to accelerate

The train that ran into the back of another in the Bedford rail crash sped up after the driver received a warning he had passed a red light, rail investigators have reported.

The driver of the East Midlands train, who died in the crash in June, acknowledged the automatic warning but did not appear to act after passing a danger signal that was rarely ever red.

Continue reading...
title: Bedford rail crash: train sped up after red light warning, say investigators

author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
description:
Indian government issued with warning it would be in contempt of court if it failed to release Jagtar Singh Johal

The British Sikh activist Jagtar Singh Johal has been released from a Delhi prison after the Indian high court warned the government it would be found in contempt of court if it continued to attempt to keep him in jail despite an 18 September court order releasing him on bail. Johal has been incarcerated for nine years without any full trial.

The court order was issued after Johal’s lawyers issued a writ of habeas corpus alleging he was being detained against the express direction of the court.

Continue reading...
title: British Sikh activist released from Delhi jail after nine-year detention

author: Associated Press
description:
One person remains missing after medical helicopter crashed off Catalina Island near Los Angeles, officials say

A medical helicopter crashed off Catalina Island near Los Angeles, killing two people and leaving two hospitalized, authorities said.

Rescuers early on Thursday searched for a fifth person who was reported to be in the aircraft and was missing, the Los Angeles county fire department said in a social media post.

Continue reading...
title: California helicopter crash kills two people and leaves two hospitalized

author: Alice Speriin New York
description:
Critics noted that the plan does not discuss Israel; others praised it for not conflating Jews with the state of Israel

When the New York City mayor, Zohran Mamdani, announced the city’s first-ever municipal strategy to address antisemitism – a nuanced, multi-pronged approach ranging from greater security measures for synagogues to an increased focus on Jewish history in public school education – critics were quick to note what the 33-page document does not mention at all: Israel.

Israel has played an outsized role in Mamdani’s campaign and since his election, with the mayor standing by his years-long support for Palestinians, an
title: Mamdani’s nuanced plan offers a roadmap to tackle antisemitism – and reignites criticism of the mayor

author: Martin Belam
description:
Netanyahu says it is too early to tell who was behind the apparent attempt to crash flight after pilot stabbed

• Don’t already get First Thing in your inbox? Sign up here

Good morning. Benjamin Netanyahu has said it is too early to tell who was behind the apparent attempt to crash a ⁠Tel Aviv-bound flydubai flight, even as Israel’s ambassador to the UN called the incident a “terror attack”. Flydubai said its flights to and from Israel would be suspended while an investigation takes place.

What is believed to have taken place in the cockpit? Pilot Smit Machchhar, an Indian citizen from Mumbai, has been hailed as a
title: First Thing: Details remain unclear after ‘terror attack’ on Dubai-Israel flight

author: David Smith in Washington
description:
Six lawmakers demand information on childcare center closures, cost changes, Head Start and government grants

Democratic senators have accused Donald Trump’s administration of worsening the country’s childcare crisis, warning that rising costs and daycare closures are leaving families with fewer affordable options.

In a letter seen by the Guardian and addressed to Alex Adams, assistant secretary of the Administration for Children and Families (ACF), senators led by Elizabeth Warren of Massachusetts argue that federal cuts and changes to childcare programs like Head Start are destabilising an already fragile system.

Continue reading...
title: Democratic senators accuse Trump administration of worsening childcare crisis

author: Tom Ambrose
description:
Bill Lee pauses state’s remaining executions for the rest of the year after inmate Christa Pike survives two lethal injections

  • Tennessee woman on death row taken to hospital after surviving two lethal injections

The Trump administration has abandoned key security bodies meant to investigate direct threats to US elections by foreign actors and domestic terrorists, according to former officials and a recent report.

While administration officials have been actively focused on unsubstantiated claims of widespread voter fraud by noncitizens, other credible election threats appear to have been overlooked, the officials say.

The latest in a series of pr
title: Tennessee governor halts executions after second botched lethal injection attempt this year – US politics live

author: Kate Connolly in Berlin
description:
• He says social media claims are ‘nonsense’ and ‘idiocy’

  • Manager sees ‘no reason to pay attention to these people’

Jürgen Klopp has reacted with disgust to a social media debate questioning whether the Germany team he is in the process of forming are “white enough”.

Klopp said he believed there was no point in giving room to “such people and their utterances”, dismissing them as “complete nonsense”.

Continue reading...
title: Jürgen Klopp disgusted by claims his Germany team are ‘not white enough’

author: George Chidi
description:
Credible threats appear to have been overlooked as administration focuses on unverified claims of voter fraud

The Trump administration has abandoned key security bodies meant to investigate direct threats to US elections by foreign actors and domestic terrorists, according to former officials and a recent report.

While administration officials have been actively focused on unsubstantiated claims of widespread voter fraud by noncitizens, other credible election threats appear to have been overlooked, the officials say.

Continue reading...
title: Trump officials abandon effort to investigate election threats, experts warn

author: Guardian community team
description:
Our wildlife series Young Country Diary is looking for articles written by children, about their autumn encounters with nature

Once again, the Young Country Diary series is open for submissions! Every three months we ask you to send us an article written by a child aged 8-14.

The article needs to be about a recent encounter they’ve had with nature – whether it’s a hedge full of berries, a beetle on the move, or a nervous deer.

Continue reading...
title: Nature boys and girls – here’s your chance to get published in the Guardian

author: Kalyeena Makortoff
description:
Deal would mark return of Canadian family to UK after it sold Selfridges department store for £4bn in 2022

  • Business live – latest updates

The private equity owner of high street pharmacy Boots is reportedly closing in on a deal to sell the business to the Canadian branch of the billionaire Weston family for $9bn (£7bn).

Sycamore Partners, which bought the wider Walgreens Boots Alliance for $23.7bn in 2025, is said to be in advanced talks with the Westons, with the Financial Times reporting that a deal could be completed as soon as next week.

Continue reading...
title: Boots owner ‘closing in on sale to Canada’s Weston family for $9bn’

author: Rob Davies
description:
Content provider part-owned by Ladbrokes, William Hill and Betfred owner signed deal with Santeda network, Casino Secrets leak reveals

Three UK bookmakers that have repeatedly warned of the dangers of the illicit market have also benefited from a lucrative deal with one of the world’s largest offshore casinos, the Guardian can reveal.

Details of the arrangement emerged as a result of last week’s Casino Secrets leak, which saw the release of thousands of confidential files held by the gambling regulator on the Caribbean island of Curaçao, a haven for offshore betting sites.

Continue reading...
title: UK bookmakers that warned over illicit market had deal with offshore casinos

author: Andrew Sparrow
description:
Tories suggest ‘tough love’ approach amid issue of one million young people not in employment, education or training

The Conservatives have also hinted that they might cut the benefits available to young people if they are living at home and their parents can support them. They are not giving many details, but this is potentially quite a big change to the way the benefits system works. At the moment young people’s eligibility for benefits depends on their own earnings and assets; if their parents can afford to subsidise them, that is not taken into account.

The Conservative party says:

The Get to Work Allowance will also put greater emphasis on family responsibility. We will review the role of family support for young adults living at home. A university student’s access to financial support can depend on their parents’ circumstances, yet the rules for young adults claiming benefits work differently. So we will look again at how parents’ earnings a
title: Badenoch proposes welfare reform that would stop many jobless under-25s getting universal credit – UK politics live

author: Tom McIlroy Political editor
description:
Greens sources say the relationship between new leader David Shoebridge and runner-up Mehreen Faruqi is seriously strained

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Sarah Hanson-Young has spoken out about major divisions in the Greens party room, offering support to newly elected leader David Shoebridge and describing politics as “brutal”.

The South Australian senator contested Wednesday’s leadership ballot, finishing behind Shoebridge and outgoing deputy leader, Mehreen Faruqi.
title: ‘Politics can be brutal’: Sarah Hanson-Young speaks out about divisions within Greens

author: Phillip Inman and Graeme Wearden
description:
Fears that US borrowing costs are unsustainable drive Britain’s 30-year bond yield to level not seen since 1998

  • Business live – latest updates

The turmoil in global bond markets intensified on Thursday amid fears that the US deficit is reaching unsustainable levels, helping drive UK long-term borrowing costs to a 28-year high.

The threat of a renewed round of inflation from the persistently high cost of oil has spooked investors, who believe central banks will be forced to raise rates in the coming months to prevent price increases from becoming embedded.
title: Global bond sell-off intensifies, as UK long-term borrowing costs pass 6%

author: Penry Buckley
description:
Major Sydney hospital also warns recent injuries from ebikes include fractures, internal bleeding, as well as ‘perforation of certain organs’

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The first illegal ebikes seized under new laws have been crushed in New South Wales, as a major Sydney hospital has warned of a spike in trauma injuries driven by those riding under the influence.

The NSW government crushed 23 ebikes at a wrecking yard in western Sydney on Thursday, turning them into scrap metal. NSW police are assessing applications for the return of an additional 13 bikes seized during a joint operation by with T
title: ‘Where illegal ebikes go to die’: first bikes seized under new laws in NSW crushed

author: Josh Butler
description:
Time magazine list includes Australian communications minister after her efforts to take on big tech

The federal communications minister, Anika Wells, has been named as one of Time magazine’s “world’s most influential rising stars” in recognition of her work on Australia’s under-16 social media ban and taking on big tech companies.

Australia’s world-leading restrictions on social media for children, which came into force last year, have garnered international attention, with governments across Europe and Asia, and in some American states, enacting or proposing similar measures.

Continue reading...
title: Anika Wells named on Time100 list as one of ‘world’s most influential rising stars’ after social media ban

author: Kalyeena Makortoff Banking correspondent
description:
Prices fell by 0.2% month on month in September as average price of a home slipped to £274,251, says Nationwide

  • Business live – latest updates

Annual house price growth halved in the UK last month, as economic uncertainty sparked by conflict in the Middle East continued to deter homebuyers.

The average price of a British home rose 0.8% in the year to September to £274,251, according to Nationwide. That was half the rate recorded in August, when house prices grew 1.6% year on year. It also marked the slowest pace of home price growth since December last year
title: UK house price growth halves amid rising mortgage interest rates

author: Anna Bawden Health and social affairs correspondent
description:
Exclusive: ADHD UK may seek judicial review of West Yorkshire NHS integrated care board’s ‘unlawful’ policy

ADHD UK has threatened legal action against an NHS organisation over its decision to impose a minimum two-year wait for attention deficit hyperactivity disorder and autism assessments.

In a legal letter to West Yorkshire NHS integrated care board (ICB), seen by the Guardian, the charity alleges that the decision to force patients to wait at least two years for such assessments was unlawful and says it will seek a judicial review if the board fails to reverse the policy.

Continue reading...
title: Charity threatens legal action over two-year NHS wait for ADHD and autism assessments

author: Tess Ikonomou
description:
Israeli embassy says the Sydney couple were on board flight that was dramatically diverted after one pilot allegedly stabbed the other

Two Australian citizens were onboard a flight to Tel Aviv that was diverted after one of the pilots allegedly stabbed the other in an attack, according to the Israeli embassy.

The passengers are a Jewish couple from Sydney, the embassy in Australia confirmed to the Guardian on Thursday. No further details were provided.

Continue reading...

description:
Some on streets of Jerusalem pledge their support to prime minister while others hope for change

On the streets of Jerusalem, crowded with secular and ultra-Orthodox Jews, religious nationalists, settlers, Palestinians, and soldiers returning from deployments, uncertainty hangs over an election less than a month away that could mark a turning point for a country profoundly changed after the Hamas attacks of 7 October 2023 and nearly three years of war in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran.

The political battle remains on a knife-edge.

title: Israelis divided as vote that could oust Netanyahu only weeks away

description:
Housemate tells court she saw the bags oozing red liquid she assumed was furniture rust

Jesse Baird’s housemate didn’t know she was looking at bags with Baird and his partner’s dead bodies, when she took a photo of oozing surfboard covers the night of their alleged murders, a court has heard.

Beau Lamarre-Condon, 31, has been accused of fatally shooting Baird and Luke Davies with his police service weapon in Baird’s Paddington home on 19 February 2024. He has pleaded not guilty to two counts of murder and one charge of aggravated break and enter.

title: Jesse Baird’s housemate did not know surfboard bags contained bodies when she took photo, court hears

Warning comes as central bank estimates fewer than one in 100 borrowers owe more on their home than its worth

The Reserve Bank says households are well placed to weather the twin storm of rising interest rates and plunging property prices, but warned that Australia would not be immune from sudden collapse of the global AI investment boom.

The central bank’s latest financial stability review – a biannual assessment of the financial system – said the “threats to global financial stability continue to mount”.

description:
Officials investigating missing persons case find bodies in remote area of Lancaster, north of Los Angeles

Law enforcement officials are looking for additional victims after two bodies were found on Tuesday in a remote area of Lancaster, California, a small city about 70 miles north of Los Angeles, the Los Angeles Times reports.

Authorities found the bodies in a shallow grave while they were investigating a missing persons case, according to KTLA. Outside of the sheriff’s department investigating the discovery of the remains as a homicide, little is known about the two people who were found in the shallow grave.

author: Associated Press
description:
Democratic governor sharply critical of Donald Trump for not passing comprehensive federal AI regulations

Governor Gavin Newsom signed laws Wednesday aimed at protecting California workers from the threats of artificial intelligence , including potential job losses and workplace surveillance.

The laws ban employers from using the technology to predict a worker’s emotional state by using their biometric data, require employers to send written notices to workers if AI is responsible for mass layoffs and ban employers from relying on AI to decide to fire someone.

title: Gavin Newsom signs laws to protect California workers from AI threat
